summary: Independently verified all three proposed facts against complete canonical OSArena.c and os.h alignment definitions; reconciled functionality document and rendered unchanged names. All thirteen non-retain dispositions are accepted: three factual corrections and ten compiled-attribution deferrals. Inherit 26 retained facts and two retained links without overrides.

proposed_facts.reason: Canonical high allocation truncates, subtracts bytes, truncates again, and stores and returns the result. The getter checks only preexisting state through source assertions. Mask arithmetic supports the qualified movement and zero-size padding explanation, not unconditional monotonicity or exhaustion handling.

Canonical low allocation rounds the start, adds bytes, rounds the end, stores the end and returns the start. There is no local capacity or arithmetic guard. The alignment definitions support the explicit alignment and non-wrapping qualifications.

The getter asserts precisely the stated sentinel and ordering predicates and returns the low boundary unchanged. Direct setters confirm that these predicates do not independently establish OSInit execution. Runtime enforcement is appropriately left unclaimed.

contradictions.reason: Accept both allocator supersessions: unconditional inward movement is not established for arbitrary unchecked inputs. The proposed explanations preserve exact operations while qualifying alignment and arithmetic assumptions.
Accept the getter supersession: explicit success predicates remove the upstream ambiguity about failure conditions without claiming compiled assertion enforcement.

Accept all five .sbss-related deferrals and all five .sdata-related deferrals listed in reviewed_contradiction_ids. Canonical declarations and uses support the named source objects' initialization, pointer types and boundary roles, but do not prove their association with compiled section targets, addresses or payload layout. No section renaming or replacement fact is warranted from this evidence.
